name: Repo Atlas
howToUse: Match the task to a category using reach_for_it_when.
Prefer repos flagged pick, and read not_for before choosing.
Use decision_rule to choose between close alternatives.
Verify activity, licence and install scripts before running anything.

categories.title: Extend your agent
categories.summary: MCP servers, skills and docs that give an AI model hands, eyes and knowledge it was never trained on.
categories.reach_for_it_when: the model has to touch a service (GitHub, a browser, a database), needs current library docs, or needs a packaged capability such as producing a .docx or .pptx
categories.decision_rule: Need current API docs: context7. Need GitHub: github-mcp-server. Need a browser: playwright-mcp. Need a repeatable procedure or document format: anthropics/skills. Building your own tool server: fastmcp. Need a server for service X: awesome-mcp-servers.

repos.what: Reference MCP servers maintained by the MCP project: filesystem, git, fetch, memory, sequential thinking and more.
repos.use_when: You want a known-good tool server, or a template for writing your own.

repos.what: Anthropic's public Agent Skills: folders of instructions and scripts that teach Claude a task, including creating .docx, .pdf, .pptx and .xlsx files.
repos.use_when: A task has a repeatable procedure (office documents, design, testing) that the agent should follow reliably.

repos.what: MCP server that pulls version-specific, up-to-date library documentation straight into the prompt.
repos.use_when: The model keeps using outdated or invented APIs for a fast-moving library.

repos.what: GitHub's official MCP server: read repositories, search code, manage issues, pull requests and Actions.
repos.use_when: The agent has to work with GitHub beyond what plain git does.

repos.what: Playwright as an MCP server: the agent drives a real browser through structured page snapshots instead of screenshots.
repos.use_when: The agent must click, fill in and verify things in a web app.

repos.what: The fast, Pythonic way to build MCP servers and clients: decorate a function and it becomes a tool.
repos.use_when: You want to expose your own script, API or database to an agent in under an hour.

repos.what: The largest curated directory of MCP servers, grouped by what they connect to.
repos.use_when: You need an MCP server for a specific service and want to see what already exists.
repos.not_for: Quality varies a lot. Read a server's source before handing it credentials.

categories.title: Let agents code
categories.summary: Agents that read a whole codebase, change it and run it, plus the tool that makes sweeping changes safe.
categories.reach_for_it_when: a task spans many files, needs to run commands and tests, or has to be handed off and left to finish
categories.decision_rule: Interactive work in the terminal: claude-code, or codex as a second opinion. Hand off a self-contained task to run unattended: OpenHands. Mechanical change across many call sites: ast-grep.

repos.what: Anthropic's agentic coding tool for the terminal: reads a codebase, edits files, runs commands, and extends through skills, hooks, subagents and MCP.
repos.use_when: You want an agent that works across a whole repository from the command line.
repos.not_for: Proprietary licence: the repository holds docs, issues and plugin examples, not the product source.

repos.what: OpenAI's open-source coding agent for the terminal: reads the repo, edits files and runs commands in a sandbox.
repos.use_when: You want a second, independent terminal agent, or you are already on OpenAI models.

repos.what: Autonomous software-engineering agent that works inside a sandbox: writes code, runs commands and browses the web.
repos.use_when: You want to hand off a self-contained task and let it run in isolation.
repos.not_for: Overkill for quick edits where a terminal agent is enough.

repos.what: Structural code search, lint and rewrite built on syntax trees instead of text, for many languages.
repos.use_when: A refactor touches hundreds of call sites and regex would be fragile.

categories.title: Reach the web
categories.summary: Fetch, drive and download from the live web, including the pages that have no API.
categories.reach_for_it_when: the answer lives on a web page, behind a login, or inside a video
categories.decision_rule: Page content as clean text: firecrawl. Unknown steps on a site with no API: browser-use. Known steps or tests: playwright. Transcript, audio or metadata from a video: yt-dlp.

repos.what: Turns websites into clean, LLM-ready markdown or structured data through crawl, scrape, search and extract APIs.
repos.use_when: An agent needs the contents of web pages, or a whole site, in readable form.

repos.what: Python library that lets an LLM operate a real browser to finish multi-step tasks on sites that have no API.
repos.use_when: The job needs logging in, clicking through and filling in forms on a site you cannot call directly.

repos.what: Reliable cross-browser automation and testing in code, for Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
repos.use_when: You need deterministic scripted browsing, scraping of JavaScript-heavy pages, or end-to-end tests.
repos.not_for: The steps are not known in advance. Use browser-use instead.

repos.what: Command-line downloader for video and audio from thousands of sites that also fetches metadata and subtitles.
repos.use_when: You need a transcript, subtitle track, audio or metadata from a video page.
repos.not_for: Only for content you have the right to download.

categories.title: Read any document
categories.summary: Turn PDFs, Office files and scans into text a model can use, and turn text back into deliverables.
categories.reach_for_it_when: the input is a file rather than text, or the output has to be a specific file format
categories.decision_rule: Any file to quick text: markitdown. Tables and layout must survive: docling. Converting between document formats: pandoc.

repos.what: Converts Office files, PDFs, images, audio, HTML and more into Markdown that language models read well.
repos.use_when: You want one call that turns almost any file into model-ready text.

repos.what: Layout-aware document parsing that keeps tables, reading order and structure from PDFs and Office files.
repos.use_when: Tables and layout matter, as in financial reports and scientific papers.

repos.what: The universal document converter: Markdown, HTML, LaTeX, docx, EPUB and dozens of other formats in either direction.
repos.use_when: You need to produce or convert a deliverable format from plain text.

categories.title: Build agents and AI apps
categories.summary: Frameworks and plumbing for putting a model inside your own product.
categories.reach_for_it_when: you are writing code that calls a model, uses tools, or has to keep state across steps
categories.decision_rule: Stateful multi-step agent: langgraph. Typed, validated outputs in Python: pydantic-ai. AI feature in a TypeScript or React app: vercel/ai. Many providers behind one API: litellm.

repos.what: Low-level framework for stateful, long-running agents modelled as graphs, with persistence and human-in-the-loop steps.
repos.use_when: You are building a multi-step agent that needs state, branching, retries and checkpoints.

repos.what: Type-safe Python agent framework from the Pydantic team: validated structured outputs and tools across model providers.
repos.use_when: You want agents with typed, validated outputs and a small API.

repos.what: The AI SDK for TypeScript: one API for text, structured output, tools and streaming UI across providers.
repos.use_when: You are adding an AI feature to a TypeScript or React web app.

repos.what: One OpenAI-style interface, as SDK or proxy, to 100+ model providers, with fallbacks and spend tracking.
repos.use_when: You want to swap or mix models without rewriting code.

categories.title: Automate and run locally
categories.summary: Run models on your own machine and wire work together so it happens without you.
categories.reach_for_it_when: the job should run on a schedule or trigger, offline, or on private data
categories.decision_rule: Triggers and glue between apps: n8n. A private or offline model: ollama. Transcribe audio: faster-whisper. Generate images or video in a repeatable pipeline: ComfyUI.

repos.what: Workflow automation with hundreds of integrations, AI nodes and a visual editor, self-hostable.
repos.use_when: You want triggers, schedules and glue between apps without writing a service.
repos.not_for: Fair-code licence, not OSI open source.

repos.what: Run open language models locally with one command and an OpenAI-compatible API.
repos.use_when: You need a private, offline or free-to-call model.

repos.what: Fast reimplementation of Whisper speech-to-text on CTranslate2.
repos.use_when: You need accurate transcripts of recordings, locally.

repos.what: Node-based engine for image, video and audio generation with a huge ecosystem of models and custom nodes.
repos.use_when: You need repeatable, scriptable image or video generation pipelines.

categories.title: Terminal superpowers
categories.summary: Small, sharp command-line tools that agents and humans both lean on every day.
categories.reach_for_it_when: you are searching, reshaping or converting things at the command line
categories.decision_rule: Find text in files: ripgrep. Run a Python script with its dependencies: uv. Reshape JSON: jq. Convert or cut audio and video: ffmpeg.

repos.what: Very fast recursive text search that respects .gitignore.
repos.use_when: Searching a large codebase or a folder of logs.

repos.what: Extremely fast Python package and project manager that also runs single-file scripts with inline dependencies.
repos.use_when: Running or sharing Python scripts without setting up an environment first.

repos.what: Command-line JSON processor for filtering, reshaping and extracting data.
repos.use_when: Taming API responses and JSON logs.

repos.what: The complete toolkit for converting, trimming, merging and processing audio and video.
repos.use_when: Any media conversion, extraction or editing task.
